title: Chapter 48: All In
content:
Chapter 48:

All in

The moment they exchanged parting words and went their separate ways, Subaru’s bravado completely peeled away.

He didn’t understand himself.

The accumulation of self-analysis he usually spent his free time on. Looking back at the results of those diagnoses, he knew exactly what kind of small-minded choices he would make in a situation like this.

And yet, he couldn’t comprehend why he was running like this now.

Since when had he become the kind of man who would do such stupid things, who would put on such a stubborn front?

Enduring pain that made him want to cry and keeping his head up just so those sisters wouldn’t feel guilty—it was completely, utterly unlike him.

Turning their backs to each other, he could tell from their footsteps that the distance between them had grown—and in that instant, Subaru’s expression collapsed.

Sharp and dull, two extremes of pain came at him incessantly. Scowling grandly, baring his teeth and sticking out his tongue,

“It hurts, it hurrrts. It hurts, Mom, Dad, Emilia-tan…!”

Calling out the names of the three major objects of dependence in his life, he shot a sideways glance at his dangling right arm.

Pain had been intermittently throbbing from it for a while now. Even though he couldn’t put any strength into it, every time it swayed, a numbness ran through him like electrodes being stabbed into his brain. He wanted to believe it was probably a dislocation.

The strike to Rem’s horn—it was an injury caused by failing his landing after delivering that blow. He should probably say that he only got off with this much because the luck of his landing spot being dirt and the luck of managing to fall on his right side had stacked together.

If he had messed up, he could have fallen on his head and had it split wide open; it wouldn’t have been strange in that situation.

Even though he had been spinning vertically, whenever he fell, it was always headfirst—he was extremely curious about what the Luck stat on his status screen was.

“This phenomenon of always falling headfirst when dropping from high places. Out of respect for Murphy’s Law, let’s name it ‘True Murphy’s Law’.”

In other words, Subaru’s headfirst falls were the fault of the as-yet-unseen Murphy-san.

Curse you, Murphy

. Thinking about stupid things like this felt like it distracted him from the pain. If it could also erase his fear of the obstacle right in front of him, that would be absolutely perfect.

Standing in the way of the running Subaru, in an encounter he had lost count of, was the puppy witchbeast.

Going beyond just being an unrepentant glutton for punishment, its vindictiveness was on a level that made him suspect it held a personal grudge against him.

“I’d really like to make this the last time with you…”

While running, Subaru braced himself, anticipating the mudslide the witchbeast would likely unleash.

If he took that completely defenseless this time, it wouldn’t end with just a dislocated right shoulder. Being KO’d into unconsciousness followed by the Predation Ending was the least painful route—he didn’t even want to imagine any other possibilities.

Shaking his head to throw off the awful imaginations, he internally simulated his footing on the animal trail and the motion of swerving to the side. The moment the mudslide triggered, he’d disregard all appearances and dash off the path.

Bring it on, he thought, turning back to face the ulgarm with half-desperate resolve,

“Hwuh?”

An idiotic, breathy voice unintentionally leaked out.

And rightfully so, because a sight that made Subaru doubt his own eyes was unfolding right there.

The puppy witchbeast let out a low growl, curling its small body even tighter. It was a gesture like it was storing up power in its entire body. Squinting to see what it would do next, Subaru’s vision was—

“—Hk!”

The furball rapidly expanded with explosive momentum.

The indoor dog that used to be a size that could fit in his hands transformed in the blink of an eye into a size where you could easily slap the label “gargantuan-tier” in front of “large dog”—Subaru’s mouth hung open,

“This is a common trope in manga and stuff, but where exactly did all that extra mass come from?”

The answer to his question was a roar that shook the forest.

It bounced up with enough force to smash the ground, supporting its rising body on its two hind legs. Then, the ulgarm clacked the claws of its free front legs together, showing off talons that looked like they could scrape bone with a single swipe.

Perhaps it was irritated that its fatal magic strikes had been evaded every single time; the final method of confrontation it chose against Subaru seemed to be directly gouging out his neck.

However,

“I have zero reason to stick around for that!”

If his memory was correct, the fangs of that puppy—former puppy—should never have reached Subaru’s body. In other words, there was no reason to risk his life trying to lift a curse from it.

That being the case, he instantly shifted to changing his route to avoid contact with it. But,

“—Ugh.”

Subaru aimed to veer off to the side and escape the frontline. Yet, as if to block his escape route, the shadows of bared-fanged witchbeasts came running up alongside him.

He quickly glanced in the opposite direction, but there were multiple shadows there as well. And what reached him from behind was the incessant sound of countless footsteps trampling the grass—.

“Geez, are you guys really that head over heels for my pheromones—damn it all!”

His role as a decoy was perfect. For the first time since being summoned to another world, Subaru had stumbled upon a calling that only he could fulfill. Though it was an honorary position he wanted to spit on and immediately return.

Once he realised, a presence enough to involuntarily make him falter in his steps enveloped his surroundings. Most likely, this was every ulgarm in this forest gathering all at once.

The fact that the sole objective of all these witchbeasts was to crush Subaru’s windpipe made his soul tremble.

Ah, seriously, honestly.

“Targeting 

me

 over the pretty sisters, your bad taste’s just demonically possessed, you guys.”

He didn’t even have the time to be terrified, tremble, or wet himself.

With his escape routes blocked, the encircling pack of witchbeasts silently forced Subaru to run straight ahead. Which meant a one-on-one duel with that giant witchbeast.

Directly in front of him, the ulgarm twisted its vicious face into something resembling an ominous smile.

A one-on-one fight that would inevitably turn into a gang beating was unavoidable; Subaru made this judgment with a sense of resignation.

—The moment he reached that conclusion, Subaru made the decision to play his trump card.

He thrust a hand into his pocket and rummaged around. The feel of a stone. The texture of crushed sweets. The discomfort of some sticky piece of cloth. And then,

“Now, I just have to believe in Puck…!”

He tossed what he had pulled out into his mouth, offering a prayer with his entire soul to the little gray cat.

He secured the round object rolling in his mouth against his back teeth, opened his eyes wide, and looked forward.

The distance between Subaru and the witchbeast was practically gone.

In less than ten seconds, they would be within reach of each other.

It was then.

“—Subaru!!”

He heard it.

Just now, he heard a voice calling Subaru’s name.

That voice had such a terribly sorrowful ring to it, filled with inescapable despair, sounding as frail as if she were witnessing the end of the world. Knowing that she was breaking her heart that much over his life or death—Subaru inadvertently found himself feeling happy.

He was way too terrible, even to himself. A pervert. A turncoat.

It wasn’t as if he couldn’t imagine what the girl who screamed his name was feeling right now, and yet, the fact that he could still smile meant he was completely out of his mind.

He laughed, fully aware of his abnormal thoughts, and with that, his smile vanished.

With his moving left hand, he readied the sword at his waist—the broken short sword, holding it at hip level.

The witchbeast’s roar came from straight ahead.

As if to drive it away, not to be outdone, Subaru also let out a furious battle cry.

His voice cracked, raising a harsh-sounding scream. However, it was a spirit that could rend silk. Glaring at each other, they clashed their very souls together.

With only the slightest moment left until contact, right before it, Subaru took a deep breath.

What he envisioned was the dead center of his body.

Between his chest and waist, in the 

tanden

-like area, he focused on the “Gate” connecting his inside and outside, and shouted.

“—Shamak!!”

Immediately after, a black cloud burst forth as if it had exploded, centered around Subaru.

With its origin point, Subaru, in the middle, it swallowed up all the witchbeasts surrounding him, plunging the decisive battle of the forest into darkness.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

—Within the black haze, a world of non-comprehension expanded.

The shape of the world, its colors, its smells—absolutely nothing could be grasped while inside it.

The only thing was the soles of his feet—only where they touched the ground conveyed a hard, certain sensation. Without that, he surely would have lost even his sense of up and down in this darkness.

Seeing nothing. Hearing nothing. Understanding nothing.

This was what it meant for the world to be in its end.

While understanding that the only certain thing within him was what was transmitted through the soles of his shoes, Subaru’s brain desperately engaged in a single task.

That was to remember.

To somehow reclaim the contents of his head that had been thoroughly swept away by the black haze, and to put whatever it was he had to do into action.

His foot left the ground to step forward, and in an instant, he lost everything.

However, comprehension returned once again when the opposite foot struck the ground in its place. The truth existed only on the soles of his shoes. Though, he could no longer tell if he was actually moving forward.

Amidst the non-comprehension, while nearly clinging to the only thing he could actually feel, Subaru’s brain rebelled against the consciousness seeking comfort, demanding to fight.

He had to take back something that was lost. If he didn’t, it would surely lead to an irreversible disaster.

Once again his foot lifted and non-comprehension arrived; the opposite foot bit the ground and comprehension returned. But this time, it felt somehow unreliable; he could tell it was slipping.

What is, what is, what is, something is missing.

Remember. The world before the non-comprehension. The world of comprehension.

What happened, and why? Who did this, and how?

For what purpose, for whose sake, what must be done to break through? Hadn’t he prepared the conditions for it?

Remember, remember, remember—.

As his brain commanded, sparks began to scatter within his thoughts.

But it wouldn’t reach. He just couldn’t grasp it entirely. He was one step away; something was missing.

A step. The foot that stepped forward wasn’t followed by the next. His feet had stopped. What was the reason for stopping? He realized that a terribly feeble, weak strength was all that resided in his legs.

Why? How come? Hadn’t he expected this?

If so, he should have prepared a means. Remember. Execute.

If the outside of his body was useless, ask the inside. Even if the outside wrapped in non-comprehension was impossible, call out to all the internal organs constantly acting on their own.

Fulfill your role, let the parts that could move, move. Complete that, and finally—.

“—!!”

Suddenly, a sensation like a blazing fire swelled up inside his body.

A passion so intense he couldn’t stand still raged within his body, and Subaru’s throat let out an inarticulate, beast-like roar. No, he thought he let one out. He didn’t even know that much.

He didn’t know. He didn’t know, but his feet began to move.

His feet gained the power to move again. Stepping forward. Thrusting his foot in what he believed was forward.

Comprehension, non-comprehension, comprehension, non-comprehension, comprehension, non-comprehension. It visited repeatedly, fading and returning, fading and returning—until eventually,

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

The moment he tore through the black haze and leapt outside, Subaru felt a tremendous sense of feedback.

An impact so strong it nearly wrenched the sword he was gripping tightly in one hand right out of his grasp.

He immediately looked around, and seeing the result of that impact, Subaru suppressed his astonishment.

The giant witchbeast, with its head still thrust into the black haze—in its torso, the short sword Subaru had been gripping was buried deeply.

The unexpected strike returned a sensation into Subaru’s hand that he had never felt before.

The feeling of driving a dull-edged blade deep into the body of a living animal. It brought Subaru a psychological shock far greater than he had imagined.

Up until now, Subaru had faced off against witchbeasts and taken their lives twice. The first was accidental, the second intentional. However, this was the very first time he had taken an action where the sensation remained so clearly in his hands.

And that gave Subaru an uncomfortableness that felt utterly out of place in this situation.

The sensation that he was currently killing a warm, living creature.

The witchbeast, still trapped in the world of non-comprehension, could not be aware of the death visiting its own body.

Looking closely, the black cloud Subaru had dashed through spanned a massive area, and not a single witchbeast’s shadow emerged from it.

Unlike Subaru, this hit them without any mental preparation whatsoever.

Once plunged into the world of non-comprehension, how could anyone laugh and call it cowardly to freeze up in the face of such unreliability?

Staggering, Subaru began a sluggish jog, trying to put distance between them while he had the chance.

His head felt heavy, his entire body sluggish. This was the effect of the debt incurred from excessive mana release, caused by Subaru—whose Gate was incompletely opened—using magic, something Puck had warned him about.

Executing that magic should normally have vomited out all the mana in his body, leaving him collapsed on the spot, unable to stand back up—yet Subaru broke through and escaped that using his trump card.

“…I’ll give you guys my thanks, brats.”

Spitting out the slightly remaining fruit peel from his mouth, Subaru muttered softly.

The fruit he spat out—it was the fruit he was tasting for the third time.

A bokko fruit. A doping item that vitalized the mana within the body and returned a slight amount of power to a depleted physical form.

God knows where they gathered it from, but it was among the useless junk the kids had given Subaru as he headed off to rescue Rem.

From the moment he confirmed its presence, this plan had vaguely existed in his head.

Had he bitten into the fruit the exact moment he invoked magic, moving might just have been possible.

It was a gamble he challenged with his life as the wager, but as for which way the scales tipped—the fact that Subaru’s life still remained in this situation was proof enough.

He aimed his feet in the direction where Ram had clearly stated the barrier was.

There was no telling how long Subaru’s Shamak—cast by an amateur with insufficient mana—would last.

He couldn’t buy any more time. Anyway, even a little closer to the barrier—.

“—Huh?”

However, that scheme of Subaru’s—

“You, bastard…”

—Was instantly derailed by a sudden claw strike that grazed his right flank.

A sharp pain heralded the bleeding, and Subaru dropped to his knees with a groan of agony. However, the enemy who had done this would not permit Subaru to kneel.

Stretching out its thick arm, it moved the limb extending blade-like claws with dexterity, lifting Subaru’s body effortlessly,

“Son of a bitch.”

Right before his eyes, a gaping maw opened wide, bringing bloodstained fangs and foul-smelling breath right to his face.

At the giant witchbeast’s obsession, Subaru laughed with desperate admiration, thinking “Bravo,”

“You’re the one who’s gonna drop dead—!”

With sheer force, he yanked out the sword lodged in its torso and drove it with all his might into that open mouth.

“—!!”

Struck by a fatal blow inside its mouth, the witchbeast flung Subaru’s body away.

In doing so, Subaru, who hadn’t let go of the sword, further ravaged the inside of its mouth with the blade. Hurled out and to the ground upon slicing its mouth into shreds, he rolled over and dropped into a forward-leaning stance.

“Yeah! What’s wrong, huh?! Bring it, you piece of shit!!”

“—!! —Hk!!”

Thrashing its head, the witchbeast directed an expression of sheer frenzy towards him.

Facing it, Subaru also shook his blood-soaked body, holding the shattered blade out in front and hurling foul-mouthed provocations.

Blood rushed to their heads; they could see nothing but each other.

His plans having been crushed time and time again, Subaru’s composure had already vanished to who-knows-where. He could no longer move forward without disposing of the vermin before his eyes.

And the same went for the other side. It, too, couldn’t process the ugly emotions swirling in its body unless it killed Subaru.

They had both entered a combat stance, ready to kick off the fight with a single trigger.

The confrontation between one person and one beast on the verge of explosion—no, two beasts—was,

“—Ul Goa.”

Forever interrupted by the direct hit of a fire projectile pouring down from the sky.

“Uwoooah?!”

Covering his face, Subaru’s body was blown backwards as he was engulfed by the impact.

Suddenly, the ground right before his eyes had exploded. The impact brought intense heat, adding burn damage to his whole body that was already covered in wounds and screaming in pain.

Cuts, bite marks, scrapes, bruises, burns, and emotional trauma—he was an absolute wreck.

“What in the world…”

Shaking his head on the dirt he’d been rolled across, Subaru groaned in pain and looked up.

And seeing the sight before him, he felt an astonishment he’d lost count of how many times he’d experienced today.

Right in front of Subaru’s eyes, the giant body of the witchbeast was bursting into flames—.

With its entire black fur engulfed in flames, the ulgarm thrashed its body, baring its agony. But the more it struggled, the more it screamed, the more the intensity of the flames increased, until eventually, the giant beast fell to the earth with a heavy thud.

Even then, it writhed in agony for a while, but that too gradually subsided, until in the end, it was nothing more than a blackened lump of meat rolling on the ground.

The unexpected end of the witchbeast—but that wasn’t all that surprised Subaru.

The fire projectile that burned the ulgarm to death—the ones raining down from the sky didn’t stop at just one, but flew in one after another, slamming into the black haze.

The sprawling darkness. From the outside, it was impossible to see what kind of power the flames that landed there unleashed.

But he could at least imagine the results.

Trapped within that unlifting darkness was the pack of witchbeasts still sunken in non-comprehension.

They wouldn’t even be able to perceive the presence of the raining fire, or notice their own bodies burning, and they would die without even understanding that their lives were lost.

Whether that was mercy or ruthlessness, Subaru no longer knew.

He didn’t know, but—

“Weell, well, you certainly used your head there~. To think you’d dare use Shamak—intended for blinding—as a marker.”

The person who had created this situation that was neither comedy nor tragedy had appeared with a frivolous smile—that much was certain.

His long indigo hair fluttering in the wind, with mismatched eyes of blue and yellow. Wrapping his tall, lanky frame in his familiar, eccentric attire, he elegantly alighted upon the witchbeast forest.

The lord of the mansion. The court mage. The useless guy who was never there when it counted—Roswaal had arrived.

He brushed the hem around his landed feet, swept his long hair over his back, and looked down at Subaru,

“Ahaa. My, My, you’re in a~awfully te~errible shape.”

“You’re way too damn late, Ros-chi. How many times do you think I had to brace myself for death?”

He figured one hand wouldn’t be enough to count.

Conscious of his mood sinking slightly as he reflected on it, Subaru nonetheless unconsciously collapsed into a sitting position out of sheer relief.

“Still, I’m surprised you knew that was me.”

“Lady Emilia ga~ave me an ea~arful about it in the village, you see. She sa~aw it coming: ‘Whether it’s reckless or foolhardy, if he’s backed into a corner, he’s sure to use magic, so don’t overlook it while you’re flying in the sky’.”

“That Beako… Emilia-tan got found out just like that.”

It seemed she lacked the capability to handle the role of keeping it perfectly hidden from Emilia.

Considering Roswaal’s miraculous intervention happened precisely because of that, perhaps he should say all’s well that ends well.

As Subaru was reflecting on the situation like this,

“Master Roswaal—”

Detouring around the black haze and rustling the bushes, Ram made her appearance. Lending her shoulder to Rem, the moment she noticed Roswaal’s figure, her composed facade instantly melted away,

“Ram apologizes for troubling you.”

“Noot at all, it’s fine. In the fi~irst place, this incident occurred in my territory. The duty to resolve it lies with me. Rather, you’ve done quite we~ell.”

Blushing at his words of appreciation, Ram pressed a hand to her chest and nodded solemnly.

Watching their exchange from the corner of his eye, Subaru let out a deep sigh,

“—Subaru!”

Suddenly, he received a flying tackle hug from Rem, forcing a “Gweh!” out of him.

Right in front of him, right beside his face, blue hair was swaying. Meaning, he judged this to be a hug from ultra-close range; under normal circumstances, he’d rejoice at the perks of the situation, but,

“Rem, right now, everywhere on my body is… ah, my consciousness is…”

Perhaps her emotional control was failing her, as the hug was filled with all her strength.

His wounded body shrieked in pain with nothing spared, and Subaru desperately tapped Rem’s back with his free left hand to signal his agony.

But,

“You’re alive. You stayed alive for Rem. Subaru, Subaru.”

Overcome with emotion, Rem didn’t notice Subaru’s reaction.

Pressing her face into his chest, he felt the sensation of warm drops slowly soaking his chest. Ticklishness and various other emotions arrived all jumbled together, completely surpassing the processing power of Subaru’s brain.

In short,

“This, pattern, again…”

Saying so, Subaru could no longer support his own neck, and his head slumped forward.

Fading consciousness. Fading voices. At the very end,

“You should sleep now. When you wake, I shall fully express my gratitude for what you have done. —At the very least, I promise to eliminate the things threatening you.”

An earnest voice from someone, stripped of all its clownishness, vibrated against his eardrums.

Feeling a firm sense of relief from that, Subaru slowly let go of his consciousness.

Right up until the brink of falling asleep, feeling the warm sensation embracing his body, savoring the feeling of having finally managed to snatch it back from the jaws of death,

Subaru’s consciousness sank into the spring of the unconscious.
